purpose: Per-subagent model + reasoning-effort routing. Pay peak intelligence once at the orchestrator; farm everything else down the ladder.

benchmark.price: USD per reference task-run, measured locally
benchmark.note: Update prices/index here when tiers change; every rule below is derived from this table.

ladder.note: The rungs agents actually pin. Chosen by walking the lower-left convex hull of `measured`: from each rung, take the next point with the cheapest $/index-point. Points not on the hull are skipped, not because they are bad, but because a neighbour buys the same points cheaper.

dominated.reason: opus-low costs $0.01 more (+2%) and scores 9 points higher (+21%). Strictly dominated — never select it.
opus-med costs $0.05 less (-7%) and scores 1 point higher. Strictly dominated — never select it.

off_hull.reason: From opus-med it buys +1 point for $0.28. fable-high buys +3 for $0.71 ($0.237/pt) — cheaper per point and strictly more capable. Skipped.
From opus-med it buys +2 for $0.51 ($0.255/pt). fable-high buys +3 for $0.71 ($0.237/pt) — cheaper per point and one point higher. Skipped; this was the old sage tier.
Technically on the hull (+1 over fable-high for $0.37) but a peak rung that clears sage by one point is not worth an agent. oracle takes fable-xhigh (+3 over sage) instead.

marginal_cost_per_index_point.interpretation: Climbing to opus-med is cheap. Climbing past it is 5.7x more expensive per point. fable-high/xhigh must be justified per call, never defaulted. fable-max is the worst step on the board ($1.04 for one point) and is never an agent tier.

grunt.label: stupid work
grunt.definition: Retrieval and execution with no judgement call. The answer is already in the repo or in a command's stdout; the agent just has to go get it.
examples: find every file that imports X
run the test suite and report raw failures
list dependency versions / env vars / route definitions
collect and dedupe log lines around a timestamp
check whether a symbol still exists before I recommend it
mechanical exploration where the search pattern is already known

code.label: code
code.definition: Writing or changing code. Split by whether the shape of the change is already decided.

dumb.definition: The change is decided; only typing remains. No invariants at risk.
examples: apply a decided rename/codemod across N files
boilerplate, scaffolding, config, fixtures
write tests for behaviour that is already specified
port a known pattern to a new file
mechanical type/lint/error fixes

smart.definition: The change requires reasoning about correctness while writing it: invariants, concurrency, error paths, non-obvious bugs.
examples: implement a feature end to end
debug a failure whose cause is not yet known
refactor across a boundary that carries invariants
anything touching auth, money, migrations, concurrency, data loss

think.label: think
think.definition: No code produced. Deciding what should happen, or judging whether what happened is right.
examples: architecture and design tradeoffs
the orchestration turn itself (main loop)
reviewing a hard diff for correctness
adversarial verification of a claim before acting on it
final synthesis across many subagent reports
peak_only: one-shot and irreversible: migrations, public releases, security calls
a bug that has already defeated opus-med twice
the deciding judgement in a workflow whose fan-out cost dwarfs the call
ceiling_only: the user asked for max by name
nothing else — $1.04 for one index point is not a routing decision an agent gets to make

escalation.policy: Start at the cheapest plausible tier. Escalate on observed failure, never in anticipation of it.
triggers: the agent returned an empty, hedged, or self-contradictory result
its output failed verification (tests, a check, a reading of the code)
it asked a question it was supposed to answer
same tier has now failed twice on the same task
rules: One rung at a time. Skipping rungs discards the cheap tier's findings.
Pass the failed attempt down as context so the higher tier does not restart from zero.
Two failures at the same rung = escalate, do not retry a third time.
Never escalate because a task merely sounds important. Escalate because a cheaper attempt actually failed.
There is no rung above oracle. fable-max is reached only when the user names it.

main_loop.rationale: The orchestrator is the think tier and sits on the same rung as sage. xhigh buys +3 index points for +85% cost; take it deliberately, not by default.

workflow_defaults.note: Values for the Workflow tool's agent(prompt, {model, effort, agentType}).
workflow_defaults.shape: Fan out wide and cheap, converge narrow and expensive. Many grunts/chores, few sages, at most one oracle per workflow.

rules: Never select sonnet-5: opus-low dominates it on both price and index.
Never select fable-low: opus-med dominates it on both price and index.
Default a subagent to the grunt tier and let failure pull it upward.
opus-med is the ceiling for anything that writes code, unless a cheaper attempt already failed.
fable-high/xhigh do not write code. They decide and they judge.
fable-max is not a tier. It is a ceiling the user has to ask for by name.
One thinker, many limbs: a single high-tier orchestrator dispatching cheap subagents beats a fleet of expensive ones.
Effort is per-agent and overrides the global effortLevel; a haiku agent under a global xhigh session still runs cheap.
